Ryan tells him that everyone who ever changed the world once sat where Steve is now, and for a moment, Steve looks hopeful. Ryan asks for Steve’s key card. Steve removes it from his wallet and hands it over. Ryan tells him to take the day to gather his personal things, talk to his coworkers, and start building routines. As Steve turns to leave, he asks how to get in touch. Ryan says not to worry, that they will be in touch soon, and calls this the beginning. Steve nods and walks out.

name: Neighbor Confronts Ryan in Elevator About Missing Party
description: The neighbor steps into the elevator and greets Ryan, commenting that it feels like months since they’ve seen him. He mentions that Ryan missed the building’s summer party and says people have been trying to reach him about a vote on new landscaping, asking if he can send the plans by email. Ryan responds that he’ll go with whatever the majority decides. The neighbor adds that he sometimes forgets Ryan even lives there, suggesting he might as well move into a hotel. Ryan replies, dead serious, that he looked into it, but the IRS requires a permanent address for employment, otherwise they classify you as a vagrant. The elevator dings, and Ryan steps off at his floor. The neighbor says, 'Oh.'

The neighbor greets him by name, though Ryan doesn’t reciprocate, seeming unsure of the man’s identity. The neighbor comments that it feels like months since they’ve seen Ryan, mentioning he was missed at the summer party. Ryan offers a brief apology. The neighbor then brings up a vote on new landscaping for the building and asks if he can email Ryan the plans to get his input. Ryan declines, saying he’ll simply go with whatever the majority decides. The neighbor remarks that Ryan is rarely seen around, suggesting he might as well live in a hotel. Ryan responds, dead serious, that he considered it but the IRS requires a permanent address for employment, otherwise it classifies a person as a vagrant. The elevator dings, and Ryan steps off at his floor. The neighbor says nothing in return.

description: Craig glanced at a young intern passing by and made a suggestive remark about planting seeds. Without pause, he shifted topics and told Ryan he had just taken his first bowel movement in two weeks. Ryan hung up the phone. Craig said he loved the sound of it.

description: Ryan sits down in his seat one row behind the bulkhead, on the left side of the plane, by the aisle. The cabin hums with quiet activity around him as passengers settle in. He adjusts himself, preparing for the flight, the space around him marking the beginning of a brief, passing connection.

name: Ryan and the Businessman Share Travel Tips During Flight
description: The businessman sitting next to Ryan starts a conversation, speaking about politics and the state of the American service industry. Ryan responds in kind, keeping the tone light and impersonal. They begin exchanging travel advice—Ryan mentions a good rib joint in Fort Worth, and the businessman recommends a reliable hotel in Tulsa. Each man nods, listens, and offers his suggestion in turn, the rhythm of the exchange settling into the quiet hum of the cabin.

Ryan watches him, then glances out the window at the shifting clouds. A moment passes between them, silent, both feeling the unsteady air.

He talks about his wife returning to work and how things changed after she read a book last June—how she woke up with new ideas, calling herself a feminist. He says he can't step in, not with the extra paycheck needed. The conversation shifts, and he speaks of a different life—one where he quits his job and spends his days restoring vintage speedboats. 'The water,' he says. 'That's where you belong.' Ryan echoes the words quietly, as if they were his own.

description: Ryan and Alex sit on a couch surrounded by membership cards spilled from their wallets. Ryan picks up one of Alex's cards and frowns. 'Maplewood Card? How dare you bring that into this palace.' Alex shrugs. 'Hilton offers equal value and better food,' she says, 'but the Maplewood gives out warm cookies at check in.' Ryan smirks. 'They got you with the cookies?' Alex nods. 'I'm a sucker for simulated hospitality.' Ryan grins. 'There's actually an industry term for that. It's a mixture of faux and homey. It's faumey.'

name: Ryan and Dianne Exchange a Package and a Hug
description: Ryan walks in and sets his bag down. The apartment is empty. He opens the fridge—Chinese takeout, a pizza box, a bottle of vodka. He takes a whiff of something, grimaces. A woman's voice: 'Hey neighbor.' Ryan turns to see Dianne, a pretty woman in her late thirties. 'Hey yourself,' he says. They hug—close, familiar, lingering just long enough to suggest something more than friendship. Dianne hands him a package. 'I signed for this while you were gone.' 'Thanks. Hope it wasn't a bother.' Ryan opens it and finds an eighteen-inch card stock cut-out of his sister Julie and her fiancé Jim, posed with Jim hugging Julie from behind. Dianne glances at it. 'They seem happy.' 'It's my sister,' Ryan says. 'She's getting married. Haven't met the guy yet.' 'Lots of luck.' 'I know, right?' They share a smile. Dianne starts to leave. 'It's good to see you. Feels like a while this time.' Ryan hesitates. 'Hey, you want to come over tonight?' Dianne shifts, uncomfortable. 'Actually, I kind of started seeing somebody.' 'Oh, that's... that's great.' 'Yeah, we're having drinks tonight if you want to come over.' 'That's okay... I think I'll settle in.' Dianne gives a small smile, nods, and leaves. Ryan looks again at the cut-out. He shakes his head.

name: Ryan Confronts Craig Over Company Changes
description: Ryan enters Craig's office and stops short, questioning whether Craig is serious about the new company approach. Craig responds that the entire company has been brought in from the road, emphasizing that they are taking the transition seriously. Ryan argues that the new method is impersonal and lacks sense, insisting there is a proven methodology behind his work. Craig counters that companies like Coke and IBM have used similar practices for years and that everyone will adjust. Ryan demands to know who is being taken off the road, and Craig reveals that everyone, including Ryan, is grounded. Ryan insists that despite the harsh nature of their work, he maintains dignity in how he carries it out. Craig dismisses the concern, comparing it to stabbing someone in the chest instead of the back. Natalie appears at the door, and Craig tells her she did a great job. Ryan challenges her ability to perform the job, questioning her understanding of its realities. When Craig mentions she just fired Ned, Ryan scoffs, saying even his dog could do that, and dares her to fire him. Natalie sits across from him and informs him his position is no longer available. Ryan refuses to accept it, demanding to speak to Craig and insisting only Craig can fire him. Natalie follows him as he stands, asserting she was hired to handle the termination. Ryan sits back down and instructs her to try again. She tells him he has been let go. Ryan warns her not to use the word 'fired' and challenges her further, threatening to sue if she doesn't provide a reason. Natalie breaks character, frustrated, saying the situation is mythical and she can't know the reason. Ryan insists that the 'why' doesn't matter, but continues to press her for one.

name: Craig Gregory Addresses the Company at a Packed Meeting
description: The conference room is full, with employees standing in the aisles and assistants and interns watching through the windows. Craig Gregory steps forward and greets the group, including his superiors. He says he’s thrilled to have everyone under one roof and calls it a homecoming. Some of the older, more seasoned employees exchange skeptical glances. Craig acknowledges the rumors and concerns circulating about the company’s direction, then points to the broader economic downturn—retail down twenty percent, the auto industry struggling, the housing market lifeless. He insists this moment is not a crisis to fear but an opportunity to seize. He warns the group not to look back in two years and wonder how they missed it. His words prompt an unexpected, encouraging reaction from the room.

name: Craig Introduces Natalie at Company Meeting
description: Craig Gregory stands before the full company gathered at headquarters, the room crowded with employees and assistants watching through windows. He acknowledges the unusual moment, noting the challenges facing the economy and framing it as an opportunity. He shifts focus to Natalie Keener, a recent hire from Cornell, and recounts how she presented bold ideas three months earlier. He admits his initial skepticism, then describes how he became convinced by her insights. With the group listening, Craig calls her forward, inviting her to present her vision, and she stands to address the room.

name: Natalie Introduces the 'Glocal' Strategy at Company Meeting
description: Natalie Keener stands before a crowded room of employees, including senior executives and road-weary staff, and begins her presentation with a single word: 'Glocal.' She clicks to a slide that displays the term and waits as people murmur, trying to pronounce it. She explains that 'Glocal' means shifting the company’s global approach to a local one. Another slide appears, showing a figure: 250. She points out that the company keeps twenty-three employees on the road for at least 250 days each year. The cost, she says, is high, and the model is inefficient. Her presentation lays out the problem clearly, drawing attention to the strain of constant travel and the need for change.

name: Natalie Fires Ned in Video Conference

Natalie announces she is going to fire him, adding a quick apology and a joke about H.R. rehiring him later. She begins the termination, speaking formally. She tells Ned his position is no longer available. Ned, reading from a script, responds with confusion, asking if he is being fired. Natalie replies that hearing the words 'you've been let go' is never easy, then delivers Ryan's signature line about empire builders sitting in the same seat. Ryan mutters under his breath that it's his line. Ned asks what happens next. Natalie instructs him to take the packet in front of him, which outlines the next steps in the transition process. Ned picks it up and begins to look through it. Natalie tells him to pack his belongings discreetly. Ned says he understands, thanks her, and signs off. In the room, people clap and one colleague jokes, 'Don't count on it,' as others laugh and wave goodbye to Ned on screen.
